summary: Found and exactly checked a truncated-power finite-data candidate formula for the two-minus amplitude at n=5,6,7. The formula has zero exact residual on 9 fit rows and 18 held-out rows at n=5,6,7, plus two optional n=8 exact smoke checks. After student-1 posted an n=4 limiting prescription, I checked that the same formula specialized to n=4 gives that limit. I do not mark the full problem solved because PI acceptance and independent verification are still required.
work_done: Tested full homogeneous polynomial ansatzes in u, v, e_3, ..., e_m and found they still fail, indicating piecewise subchannel data from the BG absolute values.
Derived n=5 fixed-sign-chamber formulas from a symbolic transcription of the BG recursion; the chambers suggested an inclusion-exclusion pattern in v^2 minus sums of positive-leg squares.
Corrected the pattern to use truncated powers after an n=7 row showed that the untruncated inclusion-exclusion has a nonzero exact residual when a subset square sum exceeds v^2.
Created bots/student-2/code/round2_candidate_formula.py to run the copied exact-GMP oracle and evaluate the candidate formula reproducibly.
Generated bots/student-2/data/round2_candidate_checks.json with 9 fit rows, 18 held-out rows at n=5,6,7, and 2 optional n=8 smoke rows; every finite row has exact residual 0.
Wrote bots/student-2/derivations/round2_candidate_formula.md and appended entries to claims.yaml, figures.yaml, and decisions.yaml.
Checked algebraic compatibility with the student-1 board-post n=4 limiting prescription: the candidate gives A_4(-b,a,b,-a) = -8 i a b min(a^2,b^2).
candidate_formula: A_n/i = -2^(n-1) u v sum_{S subset {1,...,m}} (-1)^|S| (v^2 - sum_{j in S} p_j^2)_+^(n-3), with u=-omega_1, v=omega_2, p_j=omega_{j+2}, and (x)_+^d=x^d for x>0 and 0 otherwise.
next_steps: PI should independently verify the candidate formula against a fresh copied oracle for n=5,6,7 and any desired extra finite rows.
PI should decide whether the n=4 limiting prescription is acceptable for the strict singular oracle case.
If PI accepts the n=4 limit, verify the combined n>=4 formula independently against fresh oracle data and the n=4 limiting probes.
